question: Rule: Officers count every inmate in a housing unit at 0600, 1200, 1700 and 2200. A count is not cleared until the count sheet matches the unit roster. Situation: At 1200, Officer Diaz counts 47 inmates; the roster lists 48. What must happen next?
explanation: The rule clears a count only when the sheet matches the roster. With 47 against 48, the count cannot be cleared, so it stays open until the difference is resolved.

question: Rule: A visitor may bring in only a clear plastic bag holding car keys, an ID card and up to $20 in coins for vending machines. Which visitor may enter with the bag?
optionA: Mr. Hale, keys, ID and a phone
optionB: Ms. Park, keys, ID, $15 in coins
optionC: Ms. Owen, ID and a $20 bill
optionD: Mr. Tran, keys, ID, $25 in coins
explanation: Only coins up to $20 are allowed with keys and an ID. A phone and paper money are not on the list, and $25 is over the limit.

question: Rule: Inmates moving between buildings need a movement pass signed by a sergeant. A pass is good for 30 minutes from the time written on it. Situation: A pass reads 0910. At which time does it stop being valid?
explanation: Thirty minutes after 0910 is 0940. After that the inmate needs a new pass.

question: Rule: Keys are issued only to staff on the key log. Keys may not leave the facility. Lost keys are reported to the shift commander at once. Situation: At the end of his shift Officer Grant finds a key ring in his jacket pocket in the parking lot. What should he do?
optionA: Bring it back on his next shift
optionB: Mail it to the key control office
optionC: Give it to the next officer he sees
optionD: Return it and tell the commander
explanation: Keys may not leave the facility, and a key problem goes to the shift commander right away. Holding the keys until the next shift breaks both parts of the rule.

question: Rule: Each inmate may keep up to 6 books or magazines in the cell. Newspapers do not count toward the limit. Situation: During a cell check, which inmate is over the limit?
explanation: Lowe has 7 books and magazines together. Banks has 4, Cruz has 6 and Moss has 6, since newspapers are not counted.

question: Rule: Any inmate who refuses a meal three meals in a row is reported to the medical unit. Situation: Inmate Rhee refused breakfast and lunch, ate dinner, then refused breakfast and lunch the next day. When is a report required?
optionB: If he also refuses the next dinner
optionC: Now, since he refused four meals
explanation: The rule counts refusals in a row. Eating dinner broke the first run, so the second run reaches three only if he refuses the next dinner as well.

question: Rule: Officers must make a written log entry for every inmate movement, giving the inmate's name, number, destination and time out. Which entry meets the rule?
explanation: Only the complete entry has the name, number, destination and time. Each of the others leaves out one of the four items.

question: Rule: Telephone calls last up to 15 minutes. An inmate on phone restriction may call only an attorney. Situation: Inmate Webb is on phone restriction and asks to call his sister. What should the officer do?
optionA: Allow 15 minutes since it is family
optionB: Allow a shorter call of 5 minutes
optionC: Let him call if the sister agrees
optionD: Deny the call to his sister
explanation: A restricted inmate may call only an attorney. A family call is not allowed at any length.

question: Rule: When a fight starts, the officer calls a Code Blue on the radio, gives the location, and waits for responding staff before entering, unless a life is in danger. Situation: Two inmates are shoving in the dayroom; no one is hurt. What does the officer do first?
optionA: Radio a Code Blue and the location
explanation: The rule's first step is the radio call with the location. With no life in danger, the officer waits for help before going in.

question: Rule: Sharps such as razors are issued at 0700 and must be returned by 0730. A razor not returned by 0730 starts a unit search. Situation: At 0735, the sharps log shows 23 razors out and 22 back. What happens?
optionC: The inmate is given until noon
explanation: One razor is missing after 0730, which by the rule starts a search of the unit.

question: Rule: Inmates assigned to the kitchen report at 0430 and must pass a pat search when leaving. Situation: A kitchen worker asks to skip the search because he is late for a visit. What should the officer do?
optionA: Let him go and search him later
optionB: Send him to the visit unsearched
optionD: Have another worker vouch for him
explanation: The rule requires the search every time a kitchen worker leaves. Being late for a visit is not an exception.

question: Rule: Housing unit officers check each cell in the special watch area at least every 15 minutes and record the time of each check. Situation: The last check was at 2140. When is the next check due by?
explanation: Fifteen minutes after 2140 is 2155. A check later than that breaks the rule.

question: Rule: Property taken from a new arrival is listed on a receipt. The arrival and the officer both sign it, and the arrival gets a copy. Situation: The arrival refuses to sign. Under the rule, what is missing?
explanation: The rule needs both signatures. The officer signed and the property was listed, so the arrival's signature is the missing part.

question: Rule: Only inmates in work boots may enter the maintenance shop. Situation: Inmates Fox (sneakers), Gill (work boots), Hart (sandals) and Ives (shower shoes) arrive. Who may enter?
explanation: Only work boots are allowed. Gill is the only one wearing them.

question: Rule: A visit ends at once if a visitor passes any item to an inmate. Situation: During a visit, a mother hands her son a folded photo. What should the officer do?
optionA: Keep the photo and let it go on
optionB: Warn them and allow ten minutes
optionD: Let him keep it if it is a photo
explanation: The rule ends the visit for any item passed, with no exception for photos.

question: Rule: Outside hospital trips need two officers. The inmate wears hand and leg restraints unless the doctor orders them removed for treatment. Situation: At the hospital, a doctor asks that the leg restraints come off for an X-ray. What is allowed?
optionC: Remove them and send one officer home
explanation: The rule allows removal when the doctor orders it for treatment, and only what the doctor asked for. Two officers stay on the trip.

question: Rule: Incoming mail is opened and inspected in the inmate's presence. Legal mail is opened in front of the inmate and checked only for contraband, not read. Situation: A letter arrives from a law office. What should the officer do?
optionA: Open it before him without reading
optionB: Read it fully before handing it over
optionC: Hold it until a lawyer calls
optionD: Give it to him still sealed
explanation: Legal mail is opened in the inmate's presence and checked for contraband only. Reading it or handing it over sealed both break the rule.

question: Rule: Recreation is canceled if the outside temperature is below 20 degrees F or above 95 degrees F. Situation: On which reading does outdoor recreation go ahead?
explanation: Recreation runs from 20 to 95 degrees. Only 94 is inside the range.

question: Rule: An officer relieving a post reads the post log, counts the inmates, and checks the equipment list before the off-going officer leaves. Situation: The relieving officer arrives late, and the off-going officer wants to leave at once. What should the relieving officer do?
optionA: Let the officer go and check later
optionD: Count inmates after the officer leaves
explanation: All three steps come before the off-going officer leaves. Being late does not change the order.

question: Rule: Any staff member who finds contraband puts it in a sealed bag, labels it with the date, time, location and finder's name, and gives it to the shift sergeant. Situation: An officer finds a homemade knife in a mattress. Which step comes after sealing the bag?
optionA: Hand it to the inmate's lawyer
optionC: Show it to the unit inmates
explanation: The rule's order is seal, label, then give it to the sergeant. Labeling is the next step after sealing.

question: Rule: Commissary orders may not exceed $40 a week, and no more than 5 of any one item may be bought. Which order is allowed?
explanation: Only the $38 order with 5 soups stays within both limits. The others go over $40 or buy 6 of one item.

question: Rule: Laundry exchange is on Mondays and Thursdays. An inmate may exchange one uniform per exchange day. Situation: On a Thursday, an inmate asks to swap two uniforms. What is allowed?
explanation: Thursday is an exchange day, so one uniform can be swapped. The rule allows only one per day, with no exception for damage.

question: Rule: In a fire alarm, officers unlock cells only after the control center confirms the alarm is real. Situation: The alarm sounds, and inmates shout to be let out. The control center has not yet answered. What should the officer do?
explanation: The rule ties unlocking to confirmation from the control center. Until control answers, cells stay locked.

question: Rule: Medication is given at the medication window. The officer checks each inmate's ID card before the nurse hands out medication. Situation: An inmate arrives without his ID card. What should the officer do?
optionA: Let the nurse give it anyway
optionD: Not let the nurse give it yet
explanation: The ID check comes before medication is handed out. Without the card the check cannot be done, and officers do not hand out medication.

question: Rule: Tools are signed out on the tool board. Each tool's outline is covered by a numbered tag while it is out. At closing, every outline must be uncovered. Situation: At closing, outline 14 still has a tag on it. What does this mean?
optionD: The board needs a new outline
explanation: A covered outline means the tool is signed out. At closing that is a missing tool to account for.

question: Rule: Inmates in protective custody are escorted by one officer and kept apart from all other inmates during movement. Situation: A protective custody inmate needs to go to medical while a general population line is in the hall. What should the escort officer do?
optionB: Wait until the hall is clear
optionC: Join the line and watch closely
optionD: Ask a line inmate to escort him
explanation: Protective custody inmates are kept apart from all others during movement, so the escort waits for the hall to clear.

question: Rule: A new officer may work a post alone only after two training shifts on that post. Situation: Officer Lin has had training shifts in the gym twice and in the yard once. Where may she work alone?
explanation: She has two training shifts in the gym but only one in the yard. The rule allows her to work alone in the gym only.

question: Rule: An inmate in a cell may have one blanket, one pillow and two sheets, plus a second blanket from November 1 to March 31. Situation: On April 10, which cell is over the limit?
explanation: The second blanket is allowed only from November 1 to March 31. On April 10, Kane's two blankets are over the limit.

question: Rule: Officers write an incident report before the end of the shift in which the incident happened. Situation: An officer on the 0700 to 1500 shift stops a fight at 1450. By when is the report due?
explanation: The report is due before the shift ends, which is 1500. The other times run past the end of the shift.

question: Rule: An inmate may have visits from people on his approved visitor list only, up to 3 adults at a time. Children are not counted. Situation: Which group may visit together?
optionC: 2 listed adults and a family friend
explanation: Up to 3 approved adults may visit, and children do not count. The other groups have too many adults or someone not on the list.

question: Rule: During a lockdown, all movement stops except medical emergencies, which need a sergeant's approval. Situation: During a lockdown, an inmate has chest pain. What is needed before he is moved?
explanation: A medical emergency may move during a lockdown, but only with a sergeant's approval.

question: Rule: Officers search each cell at least once a month. Cells are searched in the order on the search schedule unless a sergeant orders a cell searched out of order. Situation: A sergeant orders cell 12 searched today, but the schedule says cell 8 is next. What happens?
explanation: A sergeant's order allows a search out of order. Cell 12 is searched as ordered, and the schedule goes on after.

question: Rule: Radios are checked at the start of each shift. A radio that fails is tagged and swapped before the officer goes to post. Situation: An officer's radio fails its check but she is needed on post now. What should she do?
optionB: Go now and swap it at lunch
optionC: Borrow a radio from an inmate
optionD: Go without a radio this once
explanation: The rule requires a failed radio to be swapped before going to post, even if the post is waiting.

question: Rule: Inmates may receive packages only in the two weeks after their birthday. Situation: Inmate Oyelaran's birthday is June 3. Which package date is accepted?
explanation: The window runs from June 3 to June 17. Only June 14 falls inside it.

question: Rule: Officers do not accept gifts from inmates or their families. Any offer is written up. Situation: An inmate's wife offers the officer homemade cookies at the visiting desk. What should the officer do?
optionA: Take them and share with staff
explanation: The rule bans the gift and requires a write-up of the offer. Declining without the write-up does only half of it.

question: Rule: If a count is wrong, officers recount. If the recount is also wrong, a census count is done by name and photo. Situation: The first count and the recount both show one inmate too many. What comes next?
optionA: A third count in the usual way
optionC: Clearing the count as it is
optionD: A census count by name and photo
explanation: Two wrong counts in a row move the officer to a census count, checking each inmate by name and photo.

question: Rule: Inmates may wear personal sweatshirts in the yard only if they are gray and have no writing. Situation: Which sweatshirt is allowed in the yard?
explanation: The sweatshirt must be gray and have no writing. Only the plain gray one meets both conditions.

question: Rule: When an inmate is moved to another cell, the officer updates the unit board, the computer roster and the count sheet. Situation: An officer moved an inmate and updated the board and computer. What is left?
explanation: The rule names three updates: board, computer roster and count sheet. Only the count sheet is left.

question: Rule: Staff assaulted by an inmate are seen by medical before writing any report. Situation: An inmate punches an officer, who is not visibly hurt and wants to write the report now. What should he do?
optionB: Skip medical, as he looks fine
explanation: The rule puts the medical visit before any report, whether or not an injury shows.

question: Rule: Inmates in the law library may stay up to 2 hours, and up to 3 if a court date is within 7 days. Situation: Inmate Pruitt has a court date in 5 days. How long may he stay?
explanation: His court date is within 7 days, so the longer limit of 3 hours applies.

question: Read the passage: Direct supervision puts an officer inside the housing unit with the inmates instead of behind a glass control booth. The officer moves around, talks with inmates, and notices tension early. Supporters say problems are handled while they are small, before they turn into fights. What advantage of direct supervision does the passage give?
optionB: Fewer officers are needed per unit
optionC: Inmates spend more time in cells
explanation: The passage says the officer notices tension early so problems are handled while small. Staffing levels and cell time are not mentioned.

question: Read the passage: At intake, each new arrival is asked about medical conditions, current medications and thoughts of self-harm. The answers go to the nurse the same day. Arrivals who report thoughts of self-harm are placed on watch until a mental health worker sees them. According to the passage, who decides when the watch can end?
explanation: The passage says arrivals stay on watch until a mental health worker sees them, but it never says who ends the watch. Choosing a person goes beyond the text.

question: Read the passage: Contraband enters facilities in many ways: thrown over fences, hidden in mail, passed during visits, or brought in by staff. Because the routes are so varied, no single search method stops all of it. Facilities combine mail screening, visit supervision, perimeter patrols and staff searches. What is the main point of the passage?
optionB: Mail screening is the best method
explanation: The passage lists many routes and concludes that methods must be combined. It never ranks the routes or the methods.

question: Read the passage: Officers who write clear reports save time later. A supervisor who can understand a report on the first reading does not need to call the officer back to explain it. Clear reports also hold up better when they are read months later in a hearing. Which benefit of clear reports does the passage NOT mention?
optionB: Better use in a later hearing
explanation: Saving time, fewer calls back and use in a hearing are all in the passage. Promotion is never mentioned.

question: Read the passage: In the unit's earned privilege system, inmates start at Level 1. After 60 days without a rule violation, they move to Level 2, which adds evening dayroom time. After 60 more days without a violation, they reach Level 3, which adds a second weekly phone call. An inmate with 90 days and no violations is at which level?
explanation: Level 2 starts at 60 days and Level 3 at 120 days. At 90 days the inmate is at Level 2.

question: Read the passage: Many officers find the first year the hardest. Shift work disturbs sleep, and the job's stress follows officers home. Officers who keep regular exercise, talk with peers and use the employee assistance program report coping better. According to the passage, which group reports coping better?
optionA: Officers who work only day shifts
explanation: The passage links coping to exercise, peer talk and the assistance program. Shift type, military service and overtime are not discussed.

question: Read the passage: A good post order tells the officer what to do, when, and how. It does not repeat the whole policy manual; it points to it. Post orders are reviewed every year and whenever the post changes, so that officers are never working from outdated steps. Why are post orders reviewed when a post changes?
optionA: So the manual can be shorter
optionB: So officers can choose their posts
explanation: The passage says reviews keep officers from working from outdated steps. A changed post makes old steps outdated.

question: Read the passage: Unit 4 has 64 beds. On Monday 58 were filled, and on Tuesday 3 inmates were released while 5 were admitted. The unit is considered crowded when more than 60 beds are filled. Based on the passage, was the unit crowded on Tuesday?
explanation: 58 minus 3 plus 5 is 60. The unit is crowded only when more than 60 beds are filled, so with exactly 60 it was not crowded.

question: Read the passage: Inmates may file a grievance about conditions or staff conduct. The grievance goes first to the unit manager, who answers within 10 working days. An inmate who disagrees may appeal to the warden within 5 working days of the answer. What happens if the unit manager does not answer?
optionB: The inmate appeals to the warden
explanation: The passage gives the answer deadline but not what happens when it is missed. Any of the other choices goes beyond the text.

question: Read the passage: Officers are taught to use the least force needed to gain control. Spoken commands come first. If they fail, officers may use physical control holds. Chemical agents are used only when holds would put officers or inmates at greater risk of injury. When may chemical agents be used, according to the passage?
optionB: If holds would risk more injury
explanation: The passage limits chemical agents to cases where holds would raise the risk of injury. Failed commands lead first to holds, not agents.

question: Read the passage: The visiting room has two officers. One checks visitors in at the desk and the other watches the tables. If the table officer must leave the room, the desk officer stops check-in until the table officer returns. Why does check-in stop?
optionA: So visitors can be searched again
optionB: So the desk officer can take a break
optionC: So the tables are not left unwatched
explanation: With the table officer gone, the desk officer must watch the tables, so check-in pauses. The passage gives no other reason.

question: Read the passage: Most violent incidents in the jail happen in the first 48 hours after arrival and in the hour before shift change. Supervisors have added an officer to the intake unit and moved staff briefings so they do not leave units short at shift change. What problem were the changes meant to address?
explanation: Both changes target the two times the passage names: the first 48 hours and the hour before shift change.

question: Read the passage: Inmates who take part in education programs are less likely to return to prison after release, studies have found. The benefit is largest for programs that lead to a credential, such as a high school equivalency diploma or a trade certificate. Which program would the passage suggest helps most?
optionA: One that ends in a trade certificate
optionB: One with the most class hours
explanation: The passage says the benefit is largest when a program leads to a credential, such as a trade certificate.

question: Read the passage: A shakedown is a thorough search of a cell or area. Officers search from top to bottom and from one side to the other so nothing is skipped. Each item is put back as it was found unless it is contraband. What does the passage say about items that are not contraband?
optionC: They are returned the next day
explanation: The passage says non-contraband items are put back as they were found.

question: Read the passage: Escorting officers walk behind and slightly to one side of the inmate, not in front. From that spot they can see the inmate's hands and react if he turns. Two officers are used for inmates with a recent assault charge. Why does the officer walk behind and to one side?
optionB: To stay out of the way of staff
optionC: To keep the hands in view
optionD: To let the inmate set the pace
explanation: The passage says that spot lets the officer see the inmate's hands and react if he turns.

question: Read the passage: In the reentry unit, inmates within six months of release attend job readiness classes, open a bank account and get a state ID card before they leave. Staff say the ID card matters most, because without it a person cannot rent housing or start most jobs. Why do staff say the ID card matters most?
optionB: It takes the longest to get
optionD: It is needed for housing and work
explanation: The passage gives the reason: without the ID card a person cannot rent housing or start most jobs.

question: Read the passage: Officers must report any sexual abuse they see, hear about, or suspect, even if the inmate asks them to keep it secret. The report goes to the shift commander, who starts the facility's response. An inmate tells an officer about abuse and asks him to tell no one. What does the passage require?
optionA: Report it to the shift commander
optionC: Report it only if it happens again
optionD: Ask the inmate to file it himself
explanation: The passage requires a report even when the inmate asks for secrecy, and it names the shift commander.

question: Read the passage: The jail switched from paper count sheets to handheld scanners that read each inmate's wristband. Counts now take about 12 minutes instead of 25, and fewer errors are found later. However, the scanners need charging, and a dead scanner forces a paper count. What drawback of the scanners does the passage mention?
explanation: The only drawback given is charging: a dead scanner forces a paper count.

question: Read the passage: An officer's log is a running record of everything that happens on post. Entries are made in ink, in time order, and never erased. A mistake is crossed out with one line and initialed, so the original can still be read. Why is a mistake crossed out with one line?
optionB: So entries stay in time order
optionD: So the sergeant can find it fast
explanation: The passage says a single line keeps the original readable.

question: Read the passage: In hot weather, the jail opens extra cooling areas, gives out more water, and checks on inmates who take medications that make heat illness more likely. Officers are trained to look for confusion, heavy sweating or no sweating at all. Which inmates get extra checks, according to the passage?
explanation: The passage names inmates whose medications raise the risk of heat illness. Age and cell location are not mentioned.

question: Read the passage: Rumors spread quickly in a housing unit and can start fights. Officers who hear a rumor about a planned fight should tell a supervisor, even if it seems unlikely. A rumor that turns out false costs little; one that is ignored can cost a life. What does the author mean by "costs little"?
optionA: Checking a false one does little harm
optionB: Rumors are cheap and easy to start in a unit
explanation: The author compares the small cost of checking a false rumor with the large cost of ignoring a true one.

question: Read the passage: Food trays are counted out of the kitchen and counted back in. A missing tray is treated as missing contraband, because tray parts can be made into weapons. The unit is not unlocked for the next activity until all trays are back. Why is a missing tray treated seriously?
optionC: The kitchen needs it back fast
explanation: The passage says tray parts can be made into weapons, so a missing tray is handled like missing contraband.

question: Read the passage: The facility uses three colors of wristband: white for general population, yellow for medical watch and red for inmates who must be kept apart from others. An officer escorting a red-band inmate sees a white-band inmate in the hallway. Based on the passage, what must the officer keep in mind?
optionA: White-band inmates need a medical check
optionC: Red-band inmates must be kept apart
explanation: Red bands mark inmates who must be kept apart from others, so the officer must keep the two separated.

question: Read the passage: Some jails let families send video messages instead of letters. Messages are screened before inmates see them, just as letters are. Officials say the main benefit is that paper, which can be soaked with drugs, no longer comes in the mail. What is the main benefit, according to officials?
explanation: The passage names one main benefit: drug-soaked paper no longer comes in the mail.

question: Read the passage: When an inmate threatens to harm himself, the officer stays with him, removes items he could use, and calls for medical and mental health staff. The officer does not leave to get help; help comes to the officer. What should the officer NOT do?
explanation: The passage says the officer does not leave; help comes to the officer. The other actions are steps the passage requires.

question: Read the passage: Inmates on work release leave each morning for jobs in the community and must be back by 1900. One who returns after 1900 without calling ahead is treated as an escapee until he is found. An inmate calls at 1830 to say his bus is late and arrives at 1915. Under the passage, is he treated as an escapee?
optionD: No, he was only 15 minutes late
explanation: The escape rule covers late returns without calling ahead. He called at 1830, so he is not treated as an escapee. The 15 minutes is not the reason.

question: Read the passage: Officers learn more by watching than by listening. An inmate may say he is fine while his hands shake and he avoids eye contact. Trained officers note such signs and ask follow-up questions instead of accepting the first answer. Which statement best sums up the passage?
optionC: Behavior can say more than words
explanation: The passage contrasts what an inmate says with what his body shows. It does not claim inmates usually lie or that eye contact shows guilt.

question: Read the passage: The jail's fire plan names a primary and a backup exit route for every unit. Officers walk both routes during training so they know them in smoke. Routes are posted inside each officer station. Where are the routes posted?
explanation: The passage says the routes are posted inside each officer station.

question: Read the passage: Count time is quiet time. Inmates stand by their bunks, radios and televisions are off, and no one moves until the count clears. Quiet makes the count faster and makes it easier to hear a problem. Which reason for quiet does the passage give?
explanation: The passage gives two reasons: faster counts and hearing problems more easily.

question: Read the passage: Officers rotate between posts every few months. Rotation keeps officers from becoming too familiar with any one group of inmates, which can lead to favors and broken rules. It also builds officers who can work any post. What risk does rotation reduce?
explanation: The passage says rotation keeps officers from becoming too familiar, which can lead to favors and broken rules.

question: Read the passage: A use of force is reviewed by three people: the shift commander, the deputy warden and a training officer. The training officer looks only at whether the techniques matched training, not whether force was justified. What does the training officer review?
optionD: Whether the report was on time
explanation: The passage limits the training officer to the techniques and says justification is not part of that review.

question: Read the passage: Many jails hold people who have not been convicted and are waiting for trial. Because they are legally innocent, they are usually housed apart from sentenced inmates when space allows. Why does the passage say they are kept apart?
explanation: The passage links separate housing to their not having been convicted. It says nothing about danger, stay length or programs.

question: Notes: Officer Bell found a phone in cell 9. Cell 9 belongs to inmate Cole. Which version is best?
optionA: Officer Bell found a phone in inmate Cole's cell 9.
optionB: Inmate Cole found a phone in Officer Bell's cell 9.
optionC: Officer Bell found inmate Cole's phone in cell 9.
optionD: A phone in cell 9 found Officer Bell and Cole.
explanation: Only this version keeps who found the phone and whose cell it was. Saying it was Cole's phone adds a fact the notes do not give.

question: Notes: The fire drill began at 1400. It ended at 1412. All inmates were accounted for. Which version is best?
optionA: The drill began at 1412, and by its end all inmates were accounted for.
optionB: The 1400 drill ended at 1412 with all inmates accounted for.
optionC: All inmates were accounted for by 1400 in the drill.
optionD: The drill lasted 14 minutes with all inmates accounted for.
explanation: It keeps both times and the result. The others swap a time, drop one, or give the wrong length (the drill took 12 minutes).

question: Notes: Inmate Day complained of chest pain. Officer Ross called medical. The nurse arrived at 0820. Which version is best?
optionA: Ross reported chest pain, so inmate Day called medical; the nurse came at 0820.
optionB: After Day reported chest pain, the nurse called Ross at 0820.
optionC: After Day reported chest pain, Ross called medical; the nurse came at 0820.
optionD: Day called medical about chest pain, and Ross arrived at 0820.
explanation: It keeps who complained, who called and when the nurse arrived. The others swap the people or the actions.

question: Notes: The visitor was turned away. She had no photo ID. She arrived at 1300. Which version is best?
optionA: The visitor turned away at 1300 had photo ID.
optionB: At 1300 the visitor showed her photo ID at the desk and was then turned away.
optionC: The visitor arrived at 1300 and the ID was turned away.
optionD: The visitor who arrived at 1300 was turned away for having no photo ID.
explanation: It keeps the time, the outcome and the reason. The others say she had ID or make the ID the thing turned away.

question: Notes: Two inmates argued in the dayroom. Officer Kim separated them. No one was injured. Which version is best?
optionA: Officer Kim separated two inmates arguing in the dayroom; no one was hurt.
optionB: Two inmates in the dayroom separated Officer Kim from the others; no one was hurt.
optionC: Officer Kim argued with two inmates in the dayroom; no one was hurt.
optionD: Two inmates argued, and Officer Kim was hurt in the dayroom.
explanation: It keeps who argued, who separated them and that no one was hurt. The others change who did what or add an injury.

question: Notes: The van left at 0900. It carried three inmates. It went to the county court. Which version is best?
optionA: At 0900 three vans left for the county court.
optionB: At 0900 the van left for the county court with three inmates.
optionC: The van left the county court at 0900, carrying three inmates back.
optionD: Three inmates left the van at the county court at 0900.
explanation: It keeps the time, the destination and the number carried. The others change the number of vans, the direction or the event.

question: Notes: Officer Patel found a missing key in the sally port. Key control got it back. Which version is best?
optionA: Officer Patel lost a key in the sally port, and later key control found the missing key.
optionB: Key control found the key in the sally port and gave it to Patel.
optionC: Officer Patel found the missing key in the sally port and returned it to key control.
optionD: Officer Patel returned to the sally port after key control lost a key.
explanation: It keeps who found the key, where, and where it went. The others reverse who lost and who found it.

question: Notes: Ruiz moved to cell 14 for medical reasons. A sergeant approved it. Which version is best?
optionA: A sergeant moved to cell 14 for medical reasons.
optionB: Ruiz approved a sergeant's medical move to cell 14.
optionC: Ruiz was moved for medical reasons and a sergeant was moved to 14.
optionD: A sergeant approved Ruiz's move to cell 14 for medical reasons.
explanation: It keeps who moved, where, why and who approved it. The others move the sergeant or make Ruiz the approver.

question: Notes: The power failed at 2210. The backup generator started at 2211. The locks stayed secure. Which version is best?
optionA: The power failed at 2210, the generator started at 2211, and the locks held.
optionB: The generator failed at 2210 and the power returned at 2211.
optionC: The locks failed when the power went at 2210, until the generator started at 2211.
optionD: The power failed at 2211 after the generator started at 2210.
explanation: It keeps both times in the right order and the secure locks. The others swap the events or say the locks failed.

question: Notes: Officer Grey searched cell 22. He found no contraband. The inmate was present. Which version is best?
optionA: Officer Grey found contraband in cell 22 with the inmate present.
optionB: With the inmate present, Officer Grey searched cell 22 and found no contraband.
optionC: The inmate searched cell 22 while Officer Grey was present.
optionD: Officer Grey searched cell 22 after the inmate had left the cell and found nothing there.
explanation: It keeps the search, the result and that the inmate was present. The others add contraband, swap roles or remove the inmate.

question: Put the sentences in the best order: 1. He walked toward the sound with his flashlight. 2. The door was secure; the noise was a loose vent. 3. At 0300 the officer heard a banging noise. 4. He then checked the cell door. Which order is best?
explanation: The noise comes first, then walking toward it, checking the door and the finding. "Then" needs the walk before it.

question: Put the sentences in the best order: 1. A pat search found a small bag of pills. 2. She asked the inmate to step aside. 3. The bag was then sealed and labeled. 4. The officer saw an inmate hide something in his sock. Which order is best?
explanation: Seeing the hidden item leads to stepping aside, the search that finds the pills, and then sealing the evidence.

question: Put the sentences in the best order: 1. The alarm sounded in Unit B. 2. The fire was put out with an extinguisher. 3. Officers then wrote a report. 4. Responding officers found smoke from a burning mattress. Which order is best?
explanation: The alarm, the finding, putting out the fire, then the report. A report always follows the event.

question: Put the sentences in the best order: 1. Finally, she asked what ID to bring. 2. A woman called to ask how to visit her brother. 3. He also gave her the visiting hours. 4. The clerk explained how to get on the visitor list. Which order is best?
explanation: The call comes first, then the clerk's first answer. "He also gave her" is the clerk's second answer, and "Finally" closes the paragraph.

question: Put the sentences in the best order: 1. A recount showed the same result. 2. He was later found hiding in the laundry. 3. As a result, the unit was locked down. 4. During the noon count, one inmate was missing. Which order is best?
explanation: The missing inmate, the recount, the lockdown that follows, and the finding. "As a result" needs the recount before it.

question: Put the sentences in the best order: 1. These steps help prevent escapes. 2. They also test the alarm sensors. 3. Officers check the fences each shift. 4. Any damage is reported at once. Which order is best?
explanation: The checks come first, "also" adds the sensor test, damage is reported, and "These steps" sums them up at the end.

question: Put the sentences in the best order: 1. An inmate became dizzy in the yard. 2. The nurse then checked his blood sugar. 3. Officers helped him to a bench. 4. He was given juice and recovered. Which order is best?
explanation: Dizziness first, then the bench, the nurse's check, and the juice that helped him recover.

question: Put the sentences in the best order: 1. Instead, he waited for backup. 2. The officer saw two inmates fighting in a cell. 3. He did not enter the cell alone. 4. Backup arrived within a minute. Which order is best?
explanation: "Instead" must follow the sentence about not entering alone, and backup arrives after he waits.

question: A hearing on a rule violation is a ___ hearing. Which spelling is correct?
explanation: Disciplinary keeps the sc of discipline and ends in -ary.

question: Watching a unit by camera is video ___. Which spelling is correct?
explanation: Surveillance has a double l after the ei and ends in -ance.

question: Which spelling is correct for the store where inmates buy items?
explanation: Commissary has a double m and a double s.

question: The fence around the facility is the ___. Which spelling is correct?
explanation: Perimeter is peri plus meter, with one r in each part.

question: An officer files a ___ report after a second incident. Which spelling is correct?
explanation: Supplementary has a double p, an e after the l, and ends in -ary.

question: Which log sentence is written correctly?
optionA: The inmates were in there cells.
optionB: The inmates were in they're cells.
optionC: The inmates was in their cells.
optionD: The inmates were in their cells.
explanation: Their shows ownership, and the plural inmates takes were.

question: Which sentence has correct agreement?
optionA: Each officer carries his or her radio.
explanation: Each officer is singular, so the verb is carries.

question: Which sentence uses neither correctly?
explanation: Neither takes a singular noun and a singular verb: neither inmate was.

question: Which sentence uses the comma correctly?
explanation: A comma may follow an opening phrase. The others put commas between parts that belong together or at the end.

question: Which sentence uses the apostrophe correctly?
explanation: One officer owns the radio, so the apostrophe goes before the s: officer's.

question: Which log entry uses the active voice?
optionB: The gate was opened by Tate.
optionD: Opening of the gate was done.
explanation: In the active voice the person acting is the subject. The others are passive, and one hides who opened the gate.

question: Which log entry states a fact rather than an opinion?
optionC: Inmate is probably on a hunger strike.
optionD: Inmate was rude for no reason.
explanation: Refusing a meal is something the officer saw. The others are guesses or judgments.

question: The sergeant ___ the officers to search the unit. Which word fits the blank?
explanation: Directed means told. The others sound similar but mean influenced, left out and completed.

question: The officer gave the inmate a ___ about his conduct. Which word fits the blank?
explanation: A warning cautions about conduct. A warrant is a court order and a waiver gives up a right.

question: Which log entry says it in the fewest words?
optionB: The inmate refused, saying no, to leave.
optionC: The inmate did refuse to go and leave.
optionD: The inmate, refusing, would not leave out.
explanation: The short version says it all. The others repeat the same idea in more words.

question: Which sentence is clearest?
optionA: Officer Ames told Officer Burke that his own shift had been changed.
optionB: Officer Ames told Officer Burke that Burke's shift was changed.
optionC: Officer Ames told Burke his shift, it was changed.
optionD: Changed was the shift Ames told Burke of.
explanation: Naming Burke removes the doubt about whose shift changed. His could mean either officer.

question: Which sentence uses the right past tense of lay?
optionA: The inmate lay the tray on the table.
optionB: The inmate lied the tray on the table.
optionC: The inmate laid the tray on the table.
optionD: The inmate layed the tray on the table.
explanation: Laid is the past tense of lay, which takes an object such as the tray. Layed is not a word.

question: Which sentence uses the right word for a count?
explanation: Fewer is used with things that can be counted, such as inmates.

question: Which sentence uses the right pronoun?
optionA: The report was given to Lt. Ford and me.
optionB: The report was given to Lt. Ford and I.
optionC: The report was given to me and Lt. Ford and I.
optionD: The report was given to Lt. Ford and myself.
explanation: After to, the object form me is correct. Drop Lt. Ford and "given to me" sounds right.

question: Which spelling is correct for items inmates may not have?
explanation: Contraband is spelled with contra and band.

question: Which sentence uses the correct word?
optionA: The noise will effect the count.
optionB: The noise will afect the count.
optionC: The noise will affect the count.
optionD: The noise will affeckt the count.
explanation: Affect is the verb meaning to influence. Effect is usually a noun.

question: Which log entry is a complete sentence?
optionA: Returned from court at 1430 with the van.
optionB: Because the inmate returned from court late.
optionC: After the court hearing ended at 1430.
optionD: The inmate returned from court at 1430.
explanation: It has a subject and a verb and stands alone. The others lack a subject or begin with a word that leaves the thought unfinished.

question: Kitchen jobs need 90 days of clean conduct. Ayers has 120 days; Boyd has 60. Who qualifies?
explanation: Only Ayers has at least 90 days of clean conduct. Boyd's 60 days fall short.

question: All inmates in Unit C are over 50. Gomez is in Unit C. Which statement must be true?
optionC: All inmates over 50 are in C
explanation: Every Unit C inmate is over 50, so Gomez is. The rule does not say every inmate over 50 lives in Unit C.

question: No inmate on medical watch may work outside. Hall works outside. What follows?
optionC: Hall is not on medical watch
explanation: If medical watch rules out outside work and Hall works outside, Hall cannot be on medical watch.

question: Inmates in the honor unit have TVs. Some inmates with TVs are in Unit F. Which statement must be true?
optionA: Unit F is the honor unit
optionB: Every Unit F inmate has a TV
optionC: Honor inmates live in Unit F
explanation: The facts allow Unit F inmates to have TVs for other reasons, so nothing about Unit F follows for certain.

question: Inmates under 25 get top bunks; those 25 and over get bottom bunks. Where does Kerr, 25, sleep?
explanation: The bottom bunk is for 25 and over, and Kerr is exactly 25.

question: Only officers with van training drive transports. Officer Lee drove today's transport. What must be true?
explanation: Only van-trained officers drive transports, so Lee must have the training.

question: A rule says inmates under 21 must attend school. Inmate Ruiz attends school. What can be concluded?
explanation: The rule says who must attend, not who may attend. Older inmates may attend too, so his age is unknown.

question: Escort rules: high-risk inmates need two officers; all others need one. Today, 3 high-risk and 4 other inmates go to court at different times. How many escort assignments of officers are needed in total?
explanation: Three high-risk escorts need 6 officer assignments and four others need 4, so 10 in total.

question: Over a month, four fights in Unit D began right after mail call. What is the most reasonable conclusion?
explanation: A repeated pattern suggests a link worth watching. It does not prove a cause or justify stopping mail.

question: Inmates on three floors say the water tastes odd after main-line plumbing work today. Most likely cause?
explanation: Complaints from several floors at once point to the shared main line that was just worked on.

question: Every time the yard closes early, phone requests double that evening. What can the officer predict?
optionA: Fewer phone requests on most nights
explanation: The pattern links early yard closing to phone demand, so another early closing points to more requests.

question: Inmate Vance says he was in the library at 1400, but the library log shows he left at 1330 and the unit log shows him back at 1410. What does this suggest?
optionB: He was in the library at 1400
optionD: His account does not match the logs
explanation: Both logs agree he was gone from 1330 to 1410, which does not fit his claim to have been in the library.

question: Four searches found missing spoons, all in cells beside the kitchen return cart. Best next step?
optionA: Watch the return cart more closely
optionC: Search every cell in the facility
optionD: Move the kitchen to another floor
explanation: The pattern points to the return cart. Closer watch there targets the likely source without punishing everyone.

question: Within two days, several inmates in one unit report itchy red marks. What is most likely?
explanation: Several people in one place with the same signs at once points to a shared cause, such as an outbreak, which medical should check.

question: Steps for a cell search: (A) remove the inmate, (B) search the cell, (C) pat search the inmate, (D) write the log entry. The rule says the inmate is searched before he leaves. Which order fits?
explanation: The pat search must come before the inmate leaves the cell, then the cell is searched and the log entry is made.

question: Codes in order of urgency are Red (fire), Blue (fight), Green (medical) and Gray (power). Red outranks Blue, Blue outranks Green, Green outranks Gray. Calls for Green and Blue come in at once. Which is answered first?
explanation: Blue outranks Green, so the fight is answered first. No Red call came in.

question: Shift change: count first, brief the relief last, and keys before the log. What is the third step?
explanation: The order is count, keys, log, brief. Signing the log is third.

question: Inmates leave for court in this order: by court time, earliest first, and by cell number when times are equal. Lane: 0900, cell 8. Moss: 0830, cell 12. Nye: 0900, cell 3. Who leaves second?
explanation: Moss has the earliest time and leaves first. Lane and Nye tie at 0900, so cell 3 (Nye) goes before cell 8.

question: Order: attorneys, then family by arrival time. Father 0905, lawyer 0910, sister 0850. Who goes last?
explanation: The lawyer goes first, then family by arrival: the sister at 0850, then the father at 0905.

question: Supplies are issued alphabetically by last name. Who receives supplies third: Quinn, Baker, Morales, Diaz?
explanation: Alphabetical order is Baker, Diaz, Morales, Quinn. Morales is third.

question: After finding a weapon: secure the area, call the sergeant, bag it, report. What follows the call?
explanation: The listed order puts bagging the item right after the call to the sergeant.

question: Meals go top tier first, then lowest cell number first. Tier 2 is the top tier. Which cell eats first?
explanation: Tier 2 is the top tier and eats first, starting with its lowest cell number.

question: During a round, which observation most needs a closer look?
optionA: An inmate reading on his bunk
optionC: A cell window covered with paper
explanation: A covered window blocks the officer's view of the cell, which is a security problem. The others are normal activities.

question: At count, an inmate is lying under a blanket and does not move when called. What should the officer suspect?
optionD: He may be ill or not there
explanation: No response at count could mean a medical problem or a dummy in the bed. The officer must see living, breathing flesh.

question: On a hot day, a kitchen worker wears a jacket and keeps one hand pocketed. What might this suggest?
explanation: A jacket in the heat and a hidden hand fit concealing an item. It calls for a search, not an assumption.

question: A noisy dayroom goes silent as an officer enters, and inmates leave one table. What might be wrong?
explanation: A sudden hush and people moving from one spot can signal trouble brewing there.

question: A gate log shows a delivery truck entered at 1000 but no exit time. What is the problem?
optionA: The driver forgot to sign in
optionC: The truck may still be inside
explanation: With no exit time, the truck is unaccounted for and could still be inside the secure area.

question: An inmate who usually eats every meal has skipped three and stays in his cell. What should the officer do?
optionA: Wait to see if it continues
explanation: A sudden change in habits can signal illness, threats or depression, so it should be reported now. Waiting can let a problem grow.

question: An officer finds a sheet tied in a loop to an air vent. What does this most likely mean?
explanation: A loop tied to a fixed point is a strong warning of self-harm, and the inmate needs immediate checks.

question: A visitor's child keeps going to the vending machine near the inmate's table. What should the officer watch for?
explanation: Repeated trips near the table could be used to pass contraband, so the officer watches the hand-offs.

question: The perimeter camera for the east fence shows a frozen image with no time change. What is the problem?
optionA: The camera lens needs a cleaning
optionC: No live view of the east fence
explanation: A frozen feed means no live view, so the fence is unwatched until someone checks it in person.

question: Two inmates who are listed as enemies are both scheduled for the same recreation period. What should happen?
optionA: Let both go and watch closely
explanation: Keep-separate inmates should not be put together. Changing one schedule fixes it without punishing others.

question: If the yard is open, the gym is closed. The gym is open. What must be true?
explanation: If an open yard means a closed gym, an open gym means the yard cannot be open.

question: Officer Pike is taller than Officer Ray. Officer Ray is taller than Officer Sims. Who is shortest?
explanation: Pike is taller than Ray, who is taller than Sims, so Sims is shortest.

question: In a row of three cells, cell 3 touches cell 2 but not cell 1. Which is in the middle?
explanation: Cell 2 touches both 1 and 3, and 1 and 3 do not touch, so cell 2 is in the middle.

question: Every officer on the night shift works 12 hours. Officer Wu works 8 hours. What follows?
optionA: Wu is on the night shift
optionD: Wu is not on the night shift
explanation: All night-shift officers work 12 hours, so an 8-hour officer is not on it. It does not say which shift Wu works.

question: Inmate A gets mail on even dates; Inmate B on dates divisible by 3. Which date suits both?
explanation: 12 is even and divisible by 3. The 9th and 15th are odd, and the 14th is not divisible by 3.

question: An inmate says he never left his cell, yet his shoes have wet mud. What is the most reasonable view?
explanation: Wet mud raises a question about his account. It does not prove anything yet, so the officer checks further.

question: All program members have a GED. Some program members work in the library. Which must be true?
optionA: All library workers have a GED
optionB: No library worker has a GED
optionC: Some library workers have a GED
optionD: All GED holders are in the program
explanation: The program members who work in the library all have a GED, so at least some library workers do.

question: A pat search shows a fresh cut along the inside of an inmate's shoe sole. What might it mean?
optionA: The shoe is simply worn out
optionD: Something may be hidden in it
explanation: A fresh, neat cut inside a sole is a common hiding spot for contraband, so the shoe should be checked closely.

question: Unit A holds 46 inmates, Unit B holds 38 and Unit C holds 51. What is the total count?
A unit had 62 inmates. Five left for court, 3 arrived, and 2 returned. What is the count?
explanation: 62 - 5 + 3 + 2 = 62. Three of the five court inmates are still out, which the three arrivals balance.

question: A transport officer drove 84, 112 and 94 miles on three tours. What was the average per tour?
Each inmate gets 3 meals a day. How many meals does a 148-inmate facility serve in one week?
explanation: 148 x 3 = 444 meals a day, and 444 x 7 = 3,108.

question: Of 240 meals, 15% must be low-sodium. How many low-sodium meals are needed?
A shift runs from 2300 to 0700. How many hours is it?
explanation: From 2300 to midnight is 1 hour, and midnight to 0700 is 7 more, so 8 hours.

question: Cells are checked at the start of a 12-hour shift, every 30 minutes, and at the end. How many checks?
explanation: 12 hours has 24 half-hour gaps, so checks at the start and every 30 minutes through the end make 25.

question: A visiting room has 18 tables with 4 chairs each. Two tables are closed. How many chairs are available?
explanation: 16 open tables x 4 chairs = 64.

question: Commissary sold 37 items at $2.25 each. What was the total?
A van holds 9 inmates. How many trips are needed to move 40 inmates?
explanation: 40 / 9 is 4.4, so 4 full trips leave 4 inmates, who need a fifth trip: 5 trips.

question: Overtime is paid at 1.5 times the base rate of $28 an hour. What is the overtime rate per hour?
explanation: 28 x 1.5 = 42 dollars an hour.

question: In a 300-bed jail, 255 beds are filled. What percent of beds are filled?
Twelve boxes hold 100 pairs of gloves each. At 45 pairs a day, how many full days will they last?
Of 22 cells on a tier, half are doubles and half singles. How many inmates fit when full?
explanation: 11 double cells hold 22 and 11 single cells hold 11, so 33 in all.

question: An officer starts a count at 1352 and clears it at 1417. How long did the count take?
explanation: From 1352 to 1400 is 8 minutes, and to 1417 is 17 more, so 25 minutes.

question: A facility uses 2,450 gallons of water a day. How much does it use in a 30-day month?
Three officers split 54 cells equally, at 8 minutes a cell. How many minutes does each officer spend?
explanation: Each officer searches 54 / 3 = 18 cells, and 18 x 8 = 144 minutes.

question: Special meals: 14 diabetic, 9 kosher, 6 vegetarian and 3 allergy-free. What share of the 32 special meals are diabetic?
A van gets 13 miles to the gallon. How many gallons does a 221-mile round trip need?
explanation: 221 / 13 = 17 gallons.

question: Phone calls are limited to 15 minutes. An inmate made 4 full calls this week. How many hours is that?
explanation: 4 x 15 = 60 minutes, which is 1 hour.

question: A unit had 18 rule violations in March and 12 in April. By what percent did violations drop?
explanation: The drop is 6, and 6 / 18 = 0.333, about 33%.

question: Laundry runs 5 loads a day, 6 days a week, 40 pounds a load. How many pounds weekly?
explanation: 5 x 6 = 30 loads, and 30 x 40 = 1,200 pounds.

question: Every 7 days served counts as 8 days. How many days are served on a 120-day sentence?
explanation: Every 7 days served counts as 8, so 120 / 8 = 15 blocks of 7 days, and 15 x 7 = 105 days.

question: Fourteen officers each work 40 hours, and three also work 6 overtime hours. What are the total hours?
explanation: 14 x 40 = 560 hours, plus 3 x 6 = 18 overtime hours, makes 578.

question: You face north in a hallway and turn right, then right again. Which way do you face?
explanation: One right turn from north faces east; a second faces south.

question: Walking east, you turn left into a hall. Which way do you walk now?
explanation: Facing east, a left turn faces north, so the last stretch runs north.

question: The kitchen is north of the gym; the gym is west of the library. Where is the library from the gym?
explanation: The gym is west of the library, so the library is east of the gym.

question: Unit B is due south of A; Unit C is due east of B. Where is C from A?
explanation: Going from A, C is both south (past B's row) and east, so it lies to the southeast.

question: Cells 1 to 10 run west to east on the north side of a hall; cells 11 to 20 run east to west across from them. Which cell faces cell 3?
explanation: Cell 3 is third from the west. Across the hall, numbers run from 11 in the east to 20 in the west, so third from the west is cell 18.

question: An officer leaves the sally port heading west, turns left, then turns left again. Which way is she heading now?
explanation: From west, a left turn faces south; another left faces east.

question: The yard is south of every unit. An officer in Unit D faces the yard. What direction is behind her?
explanation: Facing the yard means facing south, so north is behind her.

question: The route to the infirmary is 2 halls north, then 1 east. Which directions retrace those halls back?
explanation: To use the same halls, undo the last leg first: 1 hall west, then 2 halls south. Going south first would use different halls.

question: Facing east, an officer makes a quarter turn to the left. Which direction does she face?
explanation: A quarter turn left from east faces north.

question: The library is between the chapel (west end) and the gym. What is at the east end?
explanation: With the chapel at the west end and the library in the middle, the gym is at the east end.

question: You enter a dayroom from the north door. The TV is on the wall to your left. If you had come in by the south door, where would the TV be?
explanation: Entering from the north you face south, and the TV on your left is on the east wall. From the south door you face north, so the east wall is on your right.

question: Entering a cell through its west wall, an officer sees the bunk on the far wall. Which wall?
explanation: Coming in from the west wall, the far wall is the east wall.

question: A desk sits in a room's northeast corner. Entering by the west door, where is the desk?
explanation: Through the west door you face east. North is on your left, so the northeast corner is ahead and to the left.

question: A map is turned upside down so north points down. On the map, which way does east now point?
explanation: Turning the map half a turn flips east from the right side to the left.

question: An officer walks 3 halls north, 2 halls east, 3 halls south. How far is she from where she started?
explanation: The north and south legs cancel, leaving her 2 halls east of the start.

question: Tower 1 sees the north and east fences. Tower 2 sees the south fence. Which fence has no tower view?
explanation: North, east and south are covered. Only the west fence is left.

question: Facing south, an officer turns to his right. Then he turns around completely. Which way is he facing?
explanation: Turning right from south faces west; turning around faces east.

question: Intake is west of medical, and medical is west of the chapel. Which way runs the chapel-to-intake route?
explanation: Intake lies west of medical, which lies west of the chapel, so the route runs west.

question: A T-shaped hallway: the stem runs south from the main hall, which runs east to west. Standing at the bottom of the stem facing the main hall, which way is east?
explanation: At the bottom of the stem facing the main hall you face north, so east is on your right.

question: A camera in the southwest corner of the yard points toward the northeast corner. What does it look across?
explanation: From the southwest corner aimed at the northeast corner, the view crosses the yard diagonally.

question: A bunk is on the north wall and a locker on the wall opposite it. Which wall holds the locker?
explanation: The wall opposite the north wall is the south wall.

question: On a map, 1 inch equals 50 feet. The hall measures 3.5 inches. How long is the hall?
The officer station sits at the center of a round housing pod. Cell 1 is due north of it and the cells are numbered clockwise, one every 45 degrees. Which direction is cell 3 from the station?
explanation: Clockwise from north, cell 2 is northeast and cell 3 is east.

question: Facing a room's south wall, you have a window on the wall behind you. Which wall is it?
explanation: Facing south, the wall behind you is the north wall.
